```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
suppressMessages({ library(data.table); library(ggplot2) })
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
Q   <- "/project/xinhe/xsun/pumseq/pumseq_processed/psi_qtl/qtl_betabinomial"
D   <- file.path(Q, "stage1_open_questions")
S   <- fread(file.path(D, "sites.tsv"), colClasses = list(character = "ref"))
EX  <- fread(file.path(D, "examples.tsv"))
FL  <- fread(file.path(D, "farlead.tsv"), colClasses = list(character = "ref"))
FLK <- fread(file.path(Q, "untreated_covariate/firstlook_w5kb_pc3_by_site.tsv"))
FLS <- fread(file.path(Q, "untreated_covariate/firstlook_w5kb_pc3_summary.tsv"))
SC  <- fread(file.path(Q, "pc_window_selection/fold5_union_auto_noUCcalled/summary/selection_no_inheritedC.tsv"))
n_clean_q <- SC[window_kb == 5 & npcs == 3, eSites_clean_q10]
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE)
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x)
th  <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) + theme(strip.background = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
FLAG <- "#eb6834"; OTHER <- "#2a78d6"; DOSE <- c(`0` = "#bcd7f5", `1` = "#5b9be0", `2` = "#1a4f8f")
E  <- S[eSite == TRUE]
nE <- nrow(E); nIC_E <- E[inherited_C == TRUE, .N]; nT <- nrow(S); nIC_T <- S[inherited_C == TRUE, .N]
```

Both questions concern sites whose %pU may reflect something other than
genetic regulation of pseudouridylation. Each needs a decision before the final
QTL scan. Numbers are from the k x window selection scan at **5 kb, k = 3**, where
**eSites** are sites with q < 0.10 (`r nE` eSites among `r fmt(nT)` tested sites).

# Question 1: the inherited-C sites

**The issue.** pU is read out as a T-to-C change at the pU base. If a cell line
carries a C allele at that base in its genome, its reads show C whether or not
the base is modified, and the site's %pU tracks genotype. We already remove sites
with a **called** U/C variant on the pU base (1,118 sites). The untreated controls
(no chemistry, so any C is inherited) show that the problem is wider:
**1,057 of the remaining sites** have a cell line with >= 10% C at the pU base in
untreated RNA (>= 10 reads, >= 2 C reads), but no called variant. These are
presumably variants missing from the genotype calls.

## What it looks like

At an inherited-C site, the treated %pU of each cell line follows its untreated C
fraction, and both follow a nearby SNP. At an unflagged eSite the untreated C
stays near zero and the treated %pU varies on its own.

```{r ex1, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.2}
e1 <- EX[kind %in% c("inherited C", "no flag")]
e1[, `:=`(treated = C / N, untreated = fifelse(uN >= 10, uC / uN, NA_real_), dose = factor(round(dosage)))]
e1[, panel := sprintf("%s\n%s (%s, q = %.1g)", sid, lead_snp, kind, q)]
e1[, panel := factor(panel, unique(panel[order(kind != "inherited C")]))]
ggplot(e1[N > 0 & !is.na(untreated)], aes(untreated, treated, colour = dose)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(size = N), alpha = 0.85) + facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = DOSE, name = "lead-SNP dosage (counted allele)", na.value = "grey60") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 4, name = "treated reads") +
  labs(x = "untreated C fraction at the pU base", y = "treated %pU") + th
```

Each point is a cell line with >= 10 untreated reads. Dashed line: treated = untreated.

## How much of the signal it carries

```{r share, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.6}
setorder(E, perm_p); E[, rank := .I]
grp <- function(r) cut(r, c(0, 20, 50, 100, Inf), labels = c("top 20", "21-50", "51-100", sprintf("101-%d", nE)))
sh <- rbind(data.table(set = "all tested sites", n = nT, share = nIC_T / nT),
            E[, .(n = .N, share = mean(inherited_C)), by = .(set = paste("eSites", grp(rank)))])
sh[, set := factor(set, set)]
ggplot(sh, aes(set, share)) + geom_col(fill = FLAG, width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%s\n(n = %d)", pct(share), n)), vjust = -0.25, size = 3.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.12), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), labels = function(x) pct(x)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "share that are inherited-C sites") + th
```

Inherited-C sites are **`r pct(nIC_T / nT)` of tested sites but `r pct(nIC_E / nE)` of
eSites** (`r nIC_E` of `r nE`), and the share rises with significance. Setting them
aside leaves **`r E[inherited_C == FALSE, .N]` eSites** at the same q-values, or
`r n_clean_q` after recomputing q without them.

## What an untreated-C covariate does

We tested one alternative to removal. The untreated C fraction of each cell line
(standardised per site) was added to the model at the 204 eSites (q < 0.05), with
the same 100 permutations. If a site's signal is inherited C, its p-value should
weaken; otherwise it should not change.

```{r cov, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=5}
FLK[, group := fifelse(inherited_C, "inherited C", "no inherited C")]
ggplot(FLK, aes(nlp_before, nlp_after, colour = group)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linetype = 2) + geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`inherited C` = FLAG, `no inherited C` = OTHER), name = NULL) + coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "-log10 p, scan model", y = "-log10 p, with untreated C as a covariate") + th
s1 <- FLS[group == "inherited C"]; s0 <- FLS[group == "no inherited C"]
```

At inherited-C eSites the median -log10 p falls from `r s1$median_nlp_before` to
`r s1$median_nlp_after`, and `r s1$remain_eSite` of `r s1$eSites` stay significant.
At the other eSites it barely moves (`r s0$median_nlp_before` to `r s0$median_nlp_after`;
`r s0$remain_eSite` of `r s0$eSites` stay). So part of the inherited-C signal is
explained by inherited C, and part is not. In a genome-wide permutation check the
covariate model had a heavier permuted tail than the scan model, almost all of it
from 3 sites where the fit failed (in the MHC, the IGH locus and chr14:51.3 Mb).

## Options

```{r opts1}
knitr::kable(data.table(
  option = c("1. Remove all inherited-C sites", "2. Untreated C as a covariate", "3. Mask lines", "4. Mixture model", "5. Keep and flag"),
  what = c("drop the 1,057 sites (a filtered phenotype already exists)",
           "add each line's untreated C fraction to the model",
           "set the phenotype missing for lines that show inherited C at the site",
           "expected treated C = a_i + (1 - a_i) mu_i, a_i = line i's inherited fraction",
           "run as now, report inherited-C sites separately"),
  pro = c("simple and conservative", "keeps sites; tested: removes much of the artefact",
          "removes the contaminated observations only", "models the read-out directly", "no information lost"),
  con = c("loses any real pU-QTL at 9% of sites; depends on the flag thresholds",
          "fit failures at a few sites; untreated depth < 10 in 14% of entries",
          "lines with low untreated depth cannot be checked", "new model; not yet tested",
          "most eSites stay artefact-prone")),
  col.names = c("option", "what", "for", "against"))
```

**To decide:** which option is primary for the final scan (and which is a
sensitivity analysis), and whether the flag thresholds (>= 10 untreated reads,
>= 10% C, >= 2 C reads) are reasonable.

# Question 2: one-line dominance and the MHC / immunoglobulin loci

**The issue.** At some sites a **single cell line supplies most of the converted
reads**. The beta-binomial null model then cannot describe the site, and any SNP
whose genotype separates that line from the rest gives a small p-value, in real
and in permuted data alike. Problem sites of this and other kinds concentrate in
the **MHC** and the **immunoglobulin (IGH, IGK, IGL) loci**. Both regions are special in LCLs: the
cell lines are clonal B cells, so the immunoglobulin loci are rearranged
differently in each line; the MHC is highly polymorphic and maps poorly to the
reference.

## What it looks like

```{r ex2, fig.width=11, fig.height=4.2}
e2 <- EX[kind == "one line dominates"]
e2[, `:=`(pu = fifelse(N > 0, C / N, NA_real_), dose = factor(round(dosage)))]
top <- e2[which.max(C)]
e2[, line := factor(cell_line, cell_line[order(-C)])]
e2[, who := fifelse(cell_line == top$cell_line, "top cell line", "other cell lines")]
cols <- c(`top cell line` = FLAG, `other cell lines` = OTHER)
pa <- ggplot(e2, aes(line, C, fill = who)) + geom_col(width = 0.8) + scale_fill_manual(values = cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "cell lines, sorted", y = "converted reads (C)",
       title = sprintf("%s of %s converted reads from %s", fmt(top$C), fmt(sum(e2$C)), top$cell_line)) +
  th + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "none")
pb <- ggplot(e2[N > 0], aes(dose, pu, colour = who)) + geom_jitter(aes(size = N), width = 0.15, height = 0, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols, guide = "none") + scale_size_area(max_size = 4, name = "treated reads") +
  labs(x = sprintf("dosage of %s (counted allele)", e2$lead_snp[1]), y = "treated %pU",
       title = sprintf("nominal p %.1g; strongest permuted p %.1g", e2$nominal_min_p[1], e2$min_perm_p[1])) + th
gridExtra::grid.arrange(pa, pb, ncol = 2, widths = c(1, 1.15),
  top = sprintf("%s (region: %s; top-line share %.2f)", e2$sid[1], e2$region[1], e2$top_line_share[1]))
```

At this site one cell line (orange) carries almost all the converted reads. In
the real data that line shares its genotype with many others, so the site is not
significant (nominal p `r sprintf("%.1g", e2$nominal_min_p[1])`). But a permutation
that happens to place the line alone in a rare genotype group gives p =
`r sprintf("%.1g", e2$min_perm_p[1])`. The permutation null of such a site is
therefore far from what the beta-binomial assumes, and if the real genotype does
set the line apart, the real p-value is just as extreme without reflecting a
genetic effect on pseudouridylation.

## Where the permutations go wrong

For each site, the strongest p-value among its 100 permutations. Under the null,
fewer than one site in the genome is expected beyond 1e-8 (dashed line).

```{r perm, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.6}
S[, regcol := fifelse(region == "other", "elsewhere", "MHC or immunoglobulin locus")]
ggplot(S[is.finite(min_perm_p)][order(regcol == "elsewhere", decreasing = TRUE)],
       aes(top_line_share, -log10(min_perm_p), colour = regcol)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.1, alpha = 0.6) + geom_hline(yintercept = 8, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`MHC or immunoglobulin locus` = FLAG, elsewhere = OTHER), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "share of the site's converted reads from its top cell line",
       y = "-log10 (strongest permuted p)") + th
x8 <- S[min_perm_p < 1e-8]
```

`r nrow(x8)` sites have a permuted p below 1e-8. Their median top-line share is
`r sprintf("%.2f", median(x8$top_line_share))` (all sites: `r sprintf("%.2f", median(S$top_line_share, na.rm = TRUE))`),
and `r x8[region != "other", .N]` of them are in the MHC or immunoglobulin loci.

The same regions dominate the **far tail of the +/-2 Mb nominal scan**: sites
whose strongest SNP lies more than 200 kb away with nothing strong nearby.

```{r far}
f <- FL[far == TRUE & local_signal == FALSE]
knitr::kable(f[, .N, by = region][order(-N)], col.names = c("region", "sites"),
  caption = sprintf("Sites with lead p < 1e-8 whose lead SNP is > 200 kb away and with no SNP p < 1e-4 within 100 kb (%d sites).", nrow(f)))
```

## How many eSites are affected

```{r affected}
knitr::kable(data.table(
  eSites = c("all", "top-line share > 0.5", "in the MHC", "in an immunoglobulin locus", "either of the two above",
             "  ... of which also inherited C"),
  n = c(nE, E[top_line_share > 0.5, .N], E[region == "MHC", .N], E[region %in% c("IGH", "IGK", "IGL"), .N],
        E[top_line_share > 0.5 | region != "other", .N], E[(top_line_share > 0.5 | region != "other") & inherited_C == TRUE, .N])),
  col.names = c("eSites (5 kb, k = 3, q < 0.10)", "n"))
ov <- E[(top_line_share > 0.5 | region != "other")]
```

Capping the top-line share would remove only `r E[top_line_share > 0.5, .N]` eSites,
but it targets the sites that distort the permutations. The MHC holds
`r E[region == "MHC", .N]` eSites, and `r ov[inherited_C == TRUE, .N]` of the `r nrow(ov)`
flagged eSites are also inherited-C sites, so **the two questions overlap**.
Inherited C is far more common in these loci: `r pct(S[region == "MHC", mean(inherited_C)])` of
MHC sites and `r pct(S[region %in% c("IGH", "IGK", "IGL"), mean(inherited_C)])` of
immunoglobulin-locus sites, against `r pct(S[region == "other", mean(inherited_C)])` elsewhere.

## Options

```{r opts2}
knitr::kable(data.table(
  option = c("1. Cap the top-line share", "2. Exclude the MHC and immunoglobulin loci", "3. Keep and flag"),
  what = c("drop sites where one line supplies more than a set share of converted reads (e.g. 0.5)",
           "drop sites in MHC chr6:28.5-33.5 Mb, IGH chr14:105.6-106.9 Mb, IGK chr2:88.9-90.2 Mb, IGL chr22:22.0-22.9 Mb (GRCh38)",
           "run as now, report these sites separately"),
  pro = c("computable for any site; targets the mechanism", "standard practice in many QTL studies", "no information lost"),
  con = c("the threshold is arbitrary", "removes any real pU-QTLs there", "these sites distort the permutation tail and the window choice")),
  col.names = c("option", "what", "for", "against"))
```

**To decide:** whether to apply option 1, option 2, or both, before the final
scan; and for option 1, the share cut-off.

`sites.tsv`, `examples.tsv` and `farlead.tsv` in
`qtl_betabinomial/stage1_open_questions/` (made by `61.stage1_open_questions_data.R`
from the saved selection-scan, untreated-control and +/-2 Mb scan results);
covariate test: `qtl_betabinomial/untreated_covariate/`. Related pages:
